raw_response:
I am not going to spread too wide this year. My family has some off-farm work, so I still need a way of farming that we can manage without getting too rushed. I will keep the land in three parts. About 25 mu I will do the usual wheat followed by summer maize, because that is the steady money and grain. About 20 mu I will keep in cotton, because I know that crop well and if the price is decent it still helps the household. The last 15 mu I will put to spring peanut. Peanut does not need as much water as wheat, and on that piece it fits better than forcing more wheat. I only finished primary school, so I do not count things too fine. I mostly follow what worked before, what I see from neighbors, and what I can afford without leaving the house short of cash.

For wheat, I will sow in early October with improved local seed, around the same time as the village usually does. I do base fertilizer before sowing, then one more topdress at jointing if the stand looks a bit pale. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I will not water too many times unless the spring is very dry. After wheat harvest in June, I will move fast and put in summer maize on the same 25 mu with minimum tillage, because the turnaround is tight. For cotton, I will stay moderate on fertilizer, use a few irrigations if it turns dry, and spray only when insects or weeds are really showing. For peanut, I will keep inputs lower than cotton and wheat, because peanut can still give me something without pushing too much money into it. The main thing this year is steady production, not gambling on very high yield.
